narrative.overview:
Dark ink on warm cream, with brass marking only what matters. The whole product, from the marketing site to the merchant admin, is drawn from five colours. Every other shade is one of those five at partial opacity, never a new hue. src/theme.css enforces this mechanically: Tailwind's slate, gray, zinc, stone, blue, sky, green, emerald and teal scales are remapped onto navy, and violet, indigo, orange, amber, red, rose and pink onto brass. Any utility a component reaches for lands back inside the palette.

The material is paper and metal, not glass and neon. Surfaces are flat white sheets on a cream ground, lifted by soft warm shadows tinted with the navy ink. Solid buttons carry a faint top sheen and a hairline inner highlight, like pressed brass. Type is Geist throughout the admin. Instrument Serif appears only as the editorial display face on marketing and auth headlines. Density is high: the root font size is 80% (1rem = 12.8px), so the admin reads compact, with text-sm (11.2px) as the working body size.

Expression is reserved for the edges of the product. The sign-in and sign-up pages have an animated backdrop (drifting brass blobs, a dot grid that lights up under the cursor, slow rings, grain). The admin stays plain and fast to scan.
keyCharacteristics: Five colours only: ink navy, brass, light brass, paper cream, white.
Geist for everything working; Instrument Serif only for marketing/auth display headlines.
Compact density (80% root size), tabular numerals in tables and live figures.
No pills or chips: status reads as bold text with a small dot.
Tight, deliberate corners (2–14px), warm navy-tinted shadows.

rules.name: The Five Colours Rule
rules.body: No hue outside the five brand colours may appear. New shades are made by mixing a brand colour with white, black or transparency, never by adding a hex.

rules.name: The Brass Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Brass marks the action, the active item, or focus. It is not decoration and never a large fill behind text.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif is for display headlines on marketing and auth surfaces only. Admin screens are Geist from top to bottom.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every table and every [data-numeric] element uses tabular numerals so figures line up and live values don't jitter.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with ink navy (rgb 17 24 39), never stock black or grey.

dos: Do use only the five brand colours; make tints by mixing with white, black or transparency.
Do keep brass for actions, active states and focus: the 2px brass :focus-visible outline at 2px offset is the one focus treatment.
Do use Geist for all admin UI, and Instrument Serif (.display) only for marketing and auth headlines.
Do show status as bold text plus a 7px dot, with a word that names the state.
Do use tabular numerals for any figure in a table or that updates live.
Do tint shadows with ink navy, and keep resting cards at shadow-xs/shadow-sm.
Do let the assistant panel push content, not cover it.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion for every transform and ambient animation.
donts: Don't add a new hex value or rely on an unmapped Tailwind hue; every scale is remapped on purpose.
Don't use pills or chips for status or tags; the global stylesheet strips them.
Don't use stock grey or black drop shadows.
Don't put Instrument Serif in the admin.
Don't set small text in brass on cream or white (2.7–3.1:1); use ink navy for small text.
Don't rely on colour alone to tell a destructive or error state apart. The palette currently has no red, so use an icon and explicit wording.
